PULLING IT TOGETHER - Gilberto's season-high 33 points, fourth-quarter surge fuel Lions past Warriors

 January 3, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: William Haufe; bhaufe@chespub.com | Page: 28 | Section: Sports

 CENTREVILLE - With the graduation of KJ Smothers, Nate Ford and Amir Coles, and with senior big man Jai Roy yet to play this season, Queen Anne's County High boys' head basketball coach Jeff Hollis thought it might take a while for his team's experience and youth to come together.If Tuesday night was any indication, Hollis' crew is coming together just fine.
Vince Gilberto scored a season-high 33 points, including 17 in a 29-16 fourth-quarter surge that cemented a 78-56 Queen Anne's County victory over Easton.
"We lost players last year, but this year we got a lot of young players," Gilberto said.
"We got to bring them up, bring them together, being the captains and seniors of this team. And we brought them together tonight, and we got the win as a team."
The two-time defending North Bayside champion-Lions (6-1 overall, 5-0 North) held a slim 15-12 lead after the first quarter. Gilberto then started heating up, scoring Queen Anne's last 10 points of the second quarter, giving the home team a 31-21 halftime lead.
"As a shooter I get a lot of shots up during the week," said Gilberto, who finished with six 3-pointers. "So I just come out here, played confident; confident in my game, confident in my teammates. I guess it was a hot night."
But Hollis didn't necessarily think his senior sharpshooter was on fire.
"I don't think it was a hot night for him," Hollis said.
"He ran to all the right spots.
He got to where he was supposed to get, and his teammates found him. And honestly that's what I expect."
Hollace Branch's inside bucket extended Queen Anne's lead to 33-21 with 27 seconds elapsed in the third quarter. But Kahlil Batson's follow and a 3-pointer from Marshall Bailey (team-high 21 points) pulled Easton (4-3, 3-1) within 33-26 with less than a minute gone in the period.
But every time the Warriors got their deficit to under double digits, the Lions responded.
Collin Woolford (14 points) hit a layup then swished consecutive 3-pointers to give Queen Anne's a 43-31 lead with 3:36 left in the third.
Easton again whittled the lead to seven before Gilberto splashed a 3 from deep in the corner for a 46-37 lead.
The Lions carried a ninepoint advantage into the fourth, but two free throws from Diontaye Copper and back-toback baskets inside the paint from Zymier Ramirez pulled Easton with 51-46 with 6:20 left.
But Amari Baynard (13 points) converted a dish from Jadereon Thompson for a layup.
Gilberto followed with a layup, then buried two 3-pointers for a 61-46 lead that prompted an Easton timeout. But the Warriors couldn't make a serious dent in their deficit the rest of the way, as the Lions outscored Easton 27-10 over the final 5:17.
"We've been trying to do it all year," Hollis said of Queen Anne's finding the open man.
"Once again we started with a young team but now they're starting to come together.
"And I've been harping on the defense all year and today we actually came to play defense," Hollis continued. "I like what we did today."

title: Easton forfeits boys' game to Cambridge-SD
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Easton forfeits boys' game to Cambridge-SD

 January 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 721

 Read News Document

 Easton High's boys' basketball team has forfeited its game Thursday at Cambridge-South Dorchester.Thursday's girls' game between the two schools will be played as scheduled at Easton High at 4 p.m., but spectators will not be allowed to attend.
The decision to forfeit the boys' game and play the girls' game without spectators is largely connected to the Oct. 27 football game between the two schools at Easton High that was stopped with just under 7 minutes remaining in the third quarter because of altercations away from the playing field.
At that game, the Easton and Cambridge-SD coaching staffs led their teams off the field while fans were instructed to leave the stadium by school administrators and local law enforcement officers. Three teenagers were arrested following the altercations.
The pattern that is emerging — basketball games scheduled between the two schools at Easton High this season will be played without fans; basketball games slated for Cambridge-SD will be forfeited by Easton High. The issue came down to playing the game with limited spectators. Easton wanted to limit or play without spectators. Cambridge-SD wanted spectators allowed.
This past Sunday, Easton High announced on its Instagram page, "Due to events that occurred during the EHS vs. CSD football game in the Fall, we have decided not to allow spectators at our upcoming girls and boys basketball game against CSD at Easton High School. As always, safety is a top priority. We apologize for any inconvenience and thank you for your support and understanding."
On Tuesday, the administrative offices of Cambridge-South Dorchester posted a statement on its Facebook page announcing Easton's decision to forfeit Thursday's boys' game at Cambridge-SD, and the Feb. 15 girls' game slated at Cambridge-SD.
"It is with great disappointment that we must convey this news: Easton High School has decided to forfeit the upcoming girls' and boys' basketball games scheduled to be held at Cambridge South Dorchester High School on Jan. 11 and Feb. 15," the statement said. "This decision was made by Easton High School and was not influenced by Cambridge-South Dorchester High in any way."
The post went on to say, "As a result of Easton High School's prearranged decision to forfeit these games, Cambridge South Dorchester High School will be credited with the wins for both of the boys' and girls' teams. We regret that parents, spectators and community members will not have the opportunity to witness these anticipated games.
"While we extend our best wishes to Easton High School, it is essential to emphasize that safety remains our top priority. We too understand the importance of maintaining a safe and secure environment for all involved.
Cambridge-SD High School was closed Wednesday due to weather conditions. Phone calls to the office of Cambridge-SD athletic director Casey O'Bier went unanswered.
On Wednesday, Talbot County Public Schools released a second statement in an email, saying that following the football game, administrators talked with coaches, athletes and parents about safety at future events.
"TCPS made the difficult decision not to allow spectators at upcoming home basketball events against CSD," the statement read.
Home games against Cambridge-SD will be livestreamed.
The statement continued that Talbot County school administrators asked that Cambridge-SD limit spectators at their home games.
"They chose not to," according to the Talbot County schools statement.
"Because the safety of our students and staff is always our highest priority, we have decided not to travel to CSD for the boys' and girls' basketball games on Jan. 11 and Feb. 15, thereby forfeiting those games," the statement read. "We value our relationship with our Dorchester County neighbors and believe this decision is in the best interests of all of the athletes involved."
The Easton and Cambridge-SD rivalry is one of the Bayside Conference's richest, especially in football and boys' basketball.
Entering Thursday's boys contest, Cambridge-SD (7-0 overall) was sitting atop the North Bayside with a 6-0 record and bidding for its first division title since 2020. Following the Vikings are second-place Queen Anne's (6-1) and Easton (5-1). Thursday's forfeit moves the Vikings to 8-0 overall and 7-0 in the division, while Easton slips to 6-4 overall, 5-2 division.
The boys' game at Easton is scheduled for Feb. 15 and will not have spectators.
Cambridge-SD's girls enter today's game at 5-2 overall, 4-2 North, trailing division leaders Queen Anne's (7-0, 6-0) and Kent Island (6-1, 6-0). Easton's girls are currently 3-6, 3-3.
Star Democrat Reporter Natalie Jones contributed to this article.

title: Warriors quietly move past Vikings
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors quietly move past Vikings

 January 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — There were no fans in the bleachers which created somewhat of an unusual atmosphere for a midseason game."It was definitely different," Easton High senior Sisi Sama said. "It was quiet."
"It was really weird," Cambridge-South Dorchester junior standout LeAsia Todd added. "I felt like we were just at practice honestly."
Due to the altercations during the Cambridge-SD at Easton football game on Oct. 27, Thursday's girls basketball game between the two schools at Easton was played without fans.
But Warrior head coach Lesley Staehli had a pre-game message for her team.
"We just knew that we had to come out here and be as normal as possible, if that makes sense," Staehli said.
It seemed to make sense to the Warriors, who used a 13-0 second-half surge to gain separation before holding off a late Vikings' comeback bid en route to a 41-33 victory.
"With playing the national anthem at the beginning to announcing (the starting lineups) with no one in the stands, we just wanted to be as normal as possible, and just play our game," said Staehli after Easton improved to 4-6 overall, 4-3 North Bayside. "I told them coming into the game, 'We've got to play Easton ball.' We've been struggling and we come out tonight and I think this is going to be a turnaround for us for the season."
Cambridge-SD (5-3, 4-3) led only once in the first quarter, when Destiny Johnson (team-high 12 points) splashed a 3-pointer with 2:11 left in the period for a 6-5 Vikings lead.
Easton closed the opening period on a 6-0 run, and maintained a slim lead through the majority of the second quarter. Destiny Johnson and Janaya Stanley connected from beyond the 3-point arc to pull Cambridge-SD even at 20-20 with 22 seconds left in the half. But Kate Adelman (10 points) hit a mid-range shot with 11 seconds remaining, nudging the Warriors to a 22-20 halftime lead.
That advantage was gone midway through the third period, as Tejanae Ballin made a free throw before Todd (nine points) made a foul shot and converted a put-back for a 24-22 Vikings' lead. Staehli called time with 4:45 to go in the third, then watched guard Serenity Velez (game-high 18 points) hit a 3-pointer to start the Warriors' decisive 13-0 spree that ended with Velez scoring a transition layup.
"We just told them to remember to play strong like they did in the first half," Staehli said. "They were outrebounding us and outplaying us. But when we ran the floor in transition and we made them work they got tired. And we had to capitalize on them getting tired, 'cause if not we'd be in trouble."
Down 35-24, Cambridge-SD began pressing the Warriors, and ended an almost 8-minute scoring drought when Kassidy Young hit a bank shot with 4:09 left in the game. Todd's 3-point play pulled Cambridge-SD within 35-29. Destiny Johnson drilled her fourth and final 3-pointer, shaving the Warriors lead to 35-32 with 2:07 left.
But the Vikings couldn't get the ball into the low post to Todd down the stretch, frustrating head coach Shamya Johnson while allowing Easton to slowly pad its lead over the final minutes.
"They weren't even attempting a good pass to her," Coach Johnson said of her team not working the ball inside to the 6-foot-3 Todd. "She's got to work extra hard because you don't want to feed her the ball. That's crazy to me. We had the whole advantage.
"As soon as they get four or five points we're hanging our heads, not realizing the game is still just one or two possessions," Shamya Johnson continued. "You've got to finish the game and have the basketball IQ to know there was nobody on the floor that was as tall as LeAsia. And not only did you have LeAsia, you also had Azeyera (Johnson) who can post up. They weren't getting either one of them the ball."
Adelman scored a layup with 1:40 remaining to end Easton's near 4-minute scoring lull. Velez hit a pair of free throws to push Easton's lead to 39-33 with 34.5 seconds left before Adelman made two free throws for the 41-33 final.
"We wish there were fans so they could see our potential because before this game we haven't really played to our full potential," said Siang, who finished with 11 points and 16 rebounds. "We had a lot of chemistry and I think we just played together as a team today. I just tried to do whatever I could for the team."
The Vikings still figure to be a favorite in the Class 1A East Regional playoffs, but their coach knows they need to regain the form that helped them start the season 4-1.
"Energy was off," Johnson said. "But I told them 'Regardless, if you've got 100 fans in the stands or zero, you're supposed to give it your all on that court for 32 minutes. The crowd can't determine how much heart you're going to give a game.'"

 EASTON — Easton High boys head basketball coach Dionte Hynson thinks his team is beating the teams it should be defeating right now.More importantly, he thinks the Warriors are playing they way they should as the regular season pushes toward its latter stages.
Senior Ja'Kai Brooks scored a game-high 16 points and classmate James Warren finished with 13 Thursday night, as Easton rolled to its sixth consecutive victory — excluding its Jan. 11 forfeit to Cambridge-South Dorchester — with a 75-40 victory over North Dorchester on senior night.
"We put in some new stuff defensively we're working on," Hynson said after the Warriors improved to 10-4 overall, 9-2 North Bayside. "Got to get a little more sharper. Got a new starting lineup, too. I think we're playing the right way right now."
Hynson started an all senior lineup on senior night as Easton carried a 14-11 lead into the second quarter against a North Dorchester team (0-14, 0-11) that dressed only seven players due to injuries. Tahjere Pritchett (team-high 11 points) scored 30 seconds into the second quarter to pull the Eagles within 14-13.
The Warriors maintained a one-point lead midway through the second before going on a 7-0 burst that extended their lead to 23-15. Easton started its new starting lineup to open the second half, and Brooks, Marshall Bailey (10 points), Kyree Acree, Kahlil Batson, and Zymier Ramirez pieced together a dominating 23-8 run in the first six-plus minutes to build a commanding 51-26 lead.
"I like our defense," said Hynson, who watched his team's fullcourt pressure create a string of Eagle turnovers in the third. "Quick hands. We've got some speed at the guard position. We just got to tighten some stuff up and get ready for the next game."
Batson and Ramirez each scored four points in the paint in the third quarter as Easton began dominating inside. Bailey then converted a steal into a transition basket before Brooks took two more steals to the rim for a 19-point cushion.
"I like where I am," Hynson said. "We're always ready to play whoever wherever. We got (Queen Anne's) on Tuesday so we'll see what happens."
Hynson pulled his starting unit with 2 minutes remaining in the third quarter and watched his reserves outscore the Eagles 14-7 in the fourth.
North Dorchester head coach Robert Smith Jr. watched his team battle, but with only two reserves, the Eagles seemed to tire down the stretch. Jae'zeon Cephas finished with nine points and Vernon Price seven.

Lions ride 1-2 punch past Easton

 EASTON — Queen Anne's County High's Bea Holthaus and Laila Coles are one of the top freshmen combinations to hit the North Bayside hardwood in a long, long time.But Lions girls' head basketball coach Mike Kern knows there are going to be nights when his team isn't at its best.
Tuesday was shaping up to be one of those nights, as Easton went on an 8-0 run to open the second half for one-point lead. But that only seemed to wake up the Lions, who proceeded to go on a 17-3 tear to close the third quarter on the way to a 53-42 victory.
"We're young," said Kern, whose team improved to 14-0 overall, 12-0 North Bayside. "We're playing in a tough environment. We're going to have these games where we don't play our best. But will still overcome. I'm proud of them for overcoming."
Holthaus, who had a game-high 25 points to go with 13 rebounds and five blocked shots, and Coles (16 points) helped Queen Anne's build a 24-17 halftime lead.
But Easton (7-8, 7-5), which lost to the Lions by 32 on Jan. 2 in Centreville, erased that deficit in the opening two minutes of the second half. Addison Chandler (10 points) buried a 3-pointer. Sisi Sama (10 points) scored inside, hit one of two free throws, then drove the lane for a basket and a 25-24 Warriors lead.
"I thought Easton came out a little hungrier than we were tonight," Kern said. "And they out-rebounded us, which is a little disappointing. But they were going hard to the ball. I think Easton deserves a lot of credit. They did a great job on the boards. And they were getting second and third opportunities, and that's what kept them in the game. We've got to do better."
The Lions may not have done better immediately on the glass, but they improved on the scoreboard. After Kern called time with 5:45 remaining in the third, Queen Anne's returned to the floor and took control of the game, outscoring the Warriors 25-5 over the next 7-plus minutes.
Leading the charge was Holthaus, who accounted for 17 points in the surge, which included burying three baseline jumpers and a 5-for-6 effort from the foul line.
"Bea is just a phenomenal athlete," Kern said. "She's sees the court really well. She makes everybody around her better. She's very unselfish. She can go inside. She can go outside. She's an all-around player. We're lucky to have her for four years."
The same can be said of Coles, who in addition to her 16 points, totaled seven steals, five assists and five rebounds.
"Her (Holthaus) and Coles both as freshmen are just going to be amazing kids coming up," Easton head coach Lesley Staehli said.
And while Holthaus and Coles proved a formidable one-two punch, the Warriors hurt themselves with a 10-for-25 performance from the free-throw line.
"We missed 15 free throws," Staehli said. "Had we made some of them, and then stopped the turnovers; taken care of the ball a little bit better (against Coles). And then shutting Bea down a little bit with hands in her face with her shot."
Queen Anne's 17-3 surge to close the third, and an 8-2 burst to open the fourth gave it a 49-30 cushion with 6:21 remaining. Easton made the score more respectable as Chandler's third 3-pointer of the game started a 12-4 Warriors' game-ending run.

 CAMBRIDGE — It may not have been the best half of basketball Queen Anne's County High's boys team has played this season, but it was pretty close.Hollace Branch's three-point play with 1.5 seconds remaining Thursday night capped a 17-point comeback, as the Lions pulled out a 58-57 victory to stun unbeaten Cambridge-South Dorchester.
"Man, we played as a team," Queen Anne's head coach Jeff Hollis said as tears welled up in his eyes. "They played hard. That's probably the hardest we've played all year."
Cambridge-SD (13-1 overall, 11-1 North Bayside) led 36-21 at halftime and bumped that lead to 17 early in the third quarter.
Queen Anne's (12-4, 11-2), which was without leading scorer Vince Gilberto, went on a 14-4 run that was capped by Jadereon Thompson's layup with 3:09 left in the third. Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker called time, and the Vikings responded as Semay Pinder and LaShaun Moody (11 points) hit consecutive baskets, extending the lead to 44-35.
The Vikings maintained that nine-point edge at 48-39 heading into the fourth quarter. Cambridge-SD looked to be regaining control, as Moody dished to Koby Ennals for a basket, converted a steal into a layup, before Pinder scored a layup for a 54-41 lead with over 5 minutes remaining.
But the North Bayside leaders scored only three more points the rest of the game while Queen Anne's was piecing together a 17-point rally over the final 4:39, with seemingly someone different scoring every time down the floor.
DJ Smith started the rally with a bucket. Nickai Gross made a free throw. Branch scored on a left-handed drive before Amari Baynard's layup pulled Queen Anne's within 54-48 with 3:36 to play.
Cambridge-SD's Pinder missed a pair of free throws.
Queen Anne's kept closing.
Baynard buried a 3-pointer with 2:10 left, drawing the Lions within 54-51. After Cambridge-SD was whistled for a moving screen, Jimmy Holthaus (game-high 14 points) scored, making it a one-point game at 54-53 with 1:34 left.
Anthony Hughes (13 points) scored on a follow shot with 1:18 to go, nudging the Vikings' lead to 56-53. Moody converted one of two free throws with 1:06 left, making it 57-53.
But Smith drove down the right side of the lane for a basket with 41.8 seconds left, shaving the Vikings lead to 57-55. Baynard blocked a shot by Hughes, but Moody retrieved the ball and was fouled. But the senior guard missed both free throws with 15.8 seconds left.
Queen Anne's got the ball back and worked it inside to Branch who scored the tying basket and was fouled. With 1.5 seconds left, the Lions senior made the free throw to complete the three-point play.
Cambridge-SD inbounded the ball, but could not get a shot off.
"Unfortunately, we're a terrible first-half team," Hollis said. "The second half, they brought the energy and it made a difference and they started believing. You could tell.
Queen Anne's defense forced multiple turnovers during a chaotic fourth quarter.
"We've been working on defense all year," Hollis said. "And finally something must have finally hit today. I don't know. But yeah, this was definitely their best game on defense by far this year.
"We were telling them we were getting ready for the playoffs and every game means something, and they took it to heart today," Hollis continued. "I'm really proud of these guys."

 EASTON — Katie Murphy has seen it all season."They tried to shut Morgan (Quade) down. They tried to shut Avery (McCall) down," Saints Peter and Paul High's girls head basketball coach said of Worcester Prep trying to clamp down on her top two leading scorers. "We needed everybody to step up and Lucy did it."
Sophomore Lucy Rankin stepped up like never before Wednesday, notching a career-high 16 points to go with 10 rebounds for her first-ever double-double, as the Sabres romped to a 49-15 victory over Worcester Prep in an Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference clash on senior night.
"She really stepped up, 'cause when that stuff happens we need the other three (starters) to step up," Quade said of Rankin. "She did really good with that tonight."
Rankin hit two free throws to give the Sabres their first points and a 2-2 tie, scored a layup midway through the first quarter to give Sts. Peter & Paul a lead it steadily widened, then made another foul shot to cap a 17-5 first quarter for the home team.
"Our coaches told us that this would happen," said Rankin of the Mallards trying to limit Quade and McCall. "So they said I needed to step up and move the ball and drive to the basket more. Once I started to get more comfortable I loosened up a bit and started to just go with the flow. This is a surprise to me."
Rankin scored on a layup and a put-back as the Sabres outscored Worcester, 15-0, in the second quarter to take a commanding 32-5 lead into the locker room.
"She really came through," Murphy said of Rankin, who had nine first-half points. "And everybody played the role they needed to play today."
One night after losing to ESIAC rival Delmarva Christian by 10, the Sabres cranked up the defensive pressure on Worcester early in the first quarter. Sts. Peter & Paul pressed Worcester full court, creating multiple turnovers while holding the Mallards scoreless the final 14 minutes of the first half.
"We've been fine tuning the press and changing different roles and different positions, and making sure that they're cutting off that middle person," Murphy said. "They did it pretty well today. And they were jumping for balls and getting the steals."
Despite Worcester's defensive efforts, Quade and McCall each finished in double figures. Quade, the Sabres' lone senior, finished with 14 points, eight rebounds and six steals. A sophomore, McCall scored all 12 of her points in the first half, and totaled four rebounds, three steals and three blocked shots.
Worcester ended an 18-plus minute scoring drought with just under 4 minutes remaining in the third quarter, and matched the Sabres in scoring during a 7-7 third. But Sts. Peter & Paul continued to play solid half-court defense in the fourth, limiting the visitors to just one basket from the field — that coming with 4 minutes left when Sydney Mize hit a 3-pointer.
"I think today we moved the ball quicker," said Quade, comparing the Sabres' loss Tuesday to Delmarva Christian to Wednesday's rout. "I think that's what kind of killed us last night. They were trapping us and we weren't moving it fast enough to get it around their traps, and if we did we would have found the open person really easily. Today I think we definitely moved it better. And honestly with them taking me and Avery out it kind of opened it up for the other three (Rankin, Sam Murphy and Annie Albright)."
With another potential showdown with Delmarva Christian in the playoffs looming, Coach Murphy was pleased with how her team rebounded from Tuesday's loss.
"Our defense is doing very well right now," Murphy said. "Every ball is a Sabre ball. They are supposed to go after it. I'm very happy with our underclassmen because they took the lead from our starters and they were after every ball, causing a bunch of jump balls. It's probably the most jump balls we've had in a game so far. Boxing out, rebounding, looking for the open player, making sure everybody was covered, they also did very well."

 WYE MILLS — The talk surrounding St. Michaels High's boys basketball team used to be could it win just one game.That narrative has changed drastically this season. Now, as they enter the second week of February, the Saints are asking themselves can they earn a home-court playoff game?
St. Michaels kept that scenario alive Saturday afternoon, as senior Nakhi Miller scored a game-high 34 points and sophomore Johnny Mautz had 20, pacing the Saints to a 79-47 rout of Mardela in the boys opener of the Peake Challenge at Chesapeake College.
"I told them these last few games, 'No, we can't win the (North) Bayside, but you can set yourselves up to have a home game as far as the seeding goes for the playoffs,'" St. Michaels second-year head coach Boo Ricketts said. "We're not just playing to beat teams. We're playing to make progress and put ourselves in a good position as a team. This is all about the Saints."
While Perryville (12-3) and Colonel Richardson (11-7) hold the top two seeds in Class 1A East Region I, St. Michaels (6-11 overall, 4-10 North Bayside) stayed within reach of No. 3 Bohemia Manor (8-9) and just ahead of Kent County (5-11) in the region field.
"We really didn't lose any pieces from last season," Mautz said. "Just been working and it's starting to come together. I mean I think we should have more than six wins to be honest."
Mautz could certainly point toward a four-point loss to North Caroline on Dec. 12, or Thursday's loss on senior night against Gunston.
"As I tell my guys, 'We're not playing against teams this year,'" Ricketts said. "'We're playing against us. It's all about growing. It's all about progress.' They always ask me, 'Is this team good?' I said, 'We're not assessing teams. Every team is good. Let's show up and play our brand of basketball.'"
The Saints did that against Mardela (1-16), as Miller and Mautz established an early trend of attacking the rim, while helping St. Michaels build a 21-6 lead after the first quarter.
"This game we definitely made up for it," said Miller, referring to the Gunston loss. "We just have to become better. Go to practice and give 100 percent every day."
Mardela actually took a 2-0 lead before the game-clock even started because St. Michaels' Hunter Gottlieb drew a technical for dunking during pre-game warm-ups.
"No coach wants to start the game that way," Ricketts said. "So I pulled Hunter in our huddle and I said, 'If you want to dunk the ball make sure you get one in the game."
Gottlieb did just that with under 2 minutes remaining in the first half, when he got a breakaway and hammered a one-handed slam that brought the crowd to its highest volume of the opening 16 minutes and gave the Saints a 33-15 lead.
"I guess he made me eat my words," Ricketts said laughing.
Up 39-18 at halftime, Miller and Mautz continued driving to the basket in the second half. Mautz drilled one of his two 3-pointers less than 3 minutes into the third quarter, extending the Saints' cushion to 45-22. Mardela's Wyatt Livingstone answered with a trey to get the Warriors back within 20, But St. Michaels closed the third on a 16-6 run, with Miller accounting for 13 in the rally.
"It was just a team effort," Miller said.
A theme the senior guard has undoubtedly picked up from his head coach this season.
"I tell them every time we win games it's a collective effort," Ricketts said. "In the games we've won there's been no one man or two men that are showing up and doing it by themselves. The games we win is when they play together and everybody believes in it. Even our bench. That's what a basketball team is."
The Saints led 61-31 heading into the fourth quarter and watched Mautz reel off seven consecutive points, widening the lead to 68-33. The Warriors put together a 9-0 run to pull within 68-42, but wouldn't get any closer as Ricketts sat his starters late.
"I feel we can always be better," Mautz said. "There's always levels to go up, but I'm decently happy about where we're at right now. Play hard it practice, start to knock down our free throws, there's really no reason why we shouldn't make a run in the playoffs this year."

 EASTON — Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys basketball team arrived in Easton Thursday night having already won the North Bayside.The way the Vikings played, you would have thought the division title was still on the line.
Sophomore Semaj Pinder scored a team-high 19 points and four others finished in double figures, as Cambridge-SD, behind an overwhelming defense, rolled to a 79-60 victory over the Warriors.
The Vikings (19-1 overall, 15-1 North Bayside) now prepare to play Stephen Decatur for the Bayside Conference championship next Tuesday at the Wicomico County Civic Center in Salisbury.
"Old fashion butt kicking," Easton head coach Dionte Hynson said after the Warriors' second most lopsided loss of the season. "Congratulations to them. They were the better team tonight. I thought they brought a whole lot of energy. We didn't match their energy tonight. First quarter, came out, played well. And then after that."
Easton (14-6, 13-3) led 12-5 with a little over 3 minutes remaining in the first quarter. Cambridge-SD sophomore Sterling Perkins (17 points) converted a steal into a layup. Darren Belizare turned another steal into a layup. Pinder then buried a 3-pointer to forge a 12-12 tie heading into the second quarter.
Cambridge-SD continued to hound the Warriors defensively and took control of the game, outscoring Easton, 21-11 in the second quarter.
"We got a chip on our shoulder," said Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker, who was minus starting point guard LaShaun Moody. "We're the underdogs we feel like every game we're going in. There's so much negativity that goes with these C-SD boys. And they just fight and fight. They're resilient. And they represent me. I'm wild. I'm passionate. I'm full of energy."
So were the Vikings.
Easton shaved a seven-point deficit to 25-21 when sophomore guard Marshall Bailey (18 points) hit a pair of free throws with 2:36 left in the second quarter. But Perkins and junior Koby Ennals (12 points) drained back-to-back 3-pointers before a Kamarion Hall's bucket capped an 8-0 run, that helped the Vikings to a 33-23 halftime lead.
"I give all props to my assistant coaches, also my defensive coach, Ryan Waters," Tucker said. "He has those guys locked in on defense. And we've been pressuring teams for the last seven games. We're just relentless on that."
After letting a 17-point third-quarter lead get away in a 58-57 loss to Queen Anne's on Feb. 1, Cambridge-SD has reeled off seven straight wins.

title: BACK ON TOP
author: Bill Haufe
content:
BACK ON TOP

 February 21, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 SALISBURY —Many in the crowd that jammed into the Wicomico Youth & Civic Center for Tuesday night's Bayside Conference boys basketball championship between Stephen Decatur and Cambridge-South Dorchester High figured the game was a mere formality in the Seahawks' coronation as kings of the hardwood.Uh, the Vikings were not part of that crowd.
"They had Decatur beating us by 25," Cambridge-SD junior forward Koby Ennals said of Bayside forecasters.
"We were 25-point underdogs," Vikings head coach Shawn Tucker said. "But that's why you play."
Crashing the boards like every rebound carried a prize, Cambridge-SD played with a fever-like intensity from baseline to baseline en route a 70-57 victory that gave the Vikings their first outright conference title since 1996.
"We just didn't match their intensity," Decatur head coach B.J. Johnson said of the Vikings. "Congratulations to Coach Tucker and Cambridge. They just wanted it more than we did in my honest opinion."
Though Cambridge-SD shared the 2003 conference crown with Pocomoke, it had lost in its last seven trips to the Bayside final.
Many figured that string would be extended as the Class 3A Seahawks came in riding an 11-game win streak.
"Nobody in this gym but a couple of people believed that we were going to win this game. And they were probably all from up North," Tucker said after the Vikings improved to 20-1.
Cambridge-SD's fan base may have had its faith shaken early as Decatur (19-2) opened an 8-0 lead less than four minutes into the game, and carried a 16-10 lead into the second quarter.
Led by guard Anthony Hughes, Cambridge-SD started hitting the boards harder and attacking the offensive rim more in the second quarter.
"Anthony Hughes played his butt off," Tucker said. "For a 6-(foot)-1 guard, he rebounded like he was 6-foot-7. This kid just gave us everything. And that's what we've been preaching."
Baskets by Ennals (game-high 21 points) and senior guard LaShaun Moody (18 points), and two free throws from Sterling Perkins (12) pulled the Vikings even at 16-all less than two minutes into the second quarter.
Davin Chandler (15 points) put the Seahawks back in front. But Hughes (nine points) scored on a double-pump shot to tie the game, then watched Moody make a three-point play for the Vikings' first lead at 21-18.
A three-point play from Brycen Coleman (team-high 18 points) drew Decatur even at 21-21. The mercurial Moody put Cambridge-SD back in front at 23-21. But Chandler and Brogan Eastlack hit back-to-back 3-pointers for the Seahawks. Chandler then scored on a drive that stoked Decatur's fans and moved the South Bayside champs to a 29-23 lead with 1:24 left in the first half.
The Vikings seemed unfazed. Perkins hit a 3-pointer, was fouled, and hit the free throw to complete a four-point play with 46.5 seconds left. Cambridge-SD then got what Tucker considered a game-changing 3-pointer from Thomas Wilson with 19 seconds left, giving the Vikings a 30-29 halftime lead.
"The 3-pointer that Thomas Wilson hit in the first half. We went up 30-29 and I saw Decatur's body language, like 'Another guy we've got to account for?'" Tucker said. "That's when I knew."
Hughes also had a feeling.
"We held them to 29 points at the half," Hughes said. "Coach told us if we keep them at 29 like that we're going to win the game. And that's what happened."
Trybe Wise's free throw seven seconds into the second half forged the game's fourth and final tie at 30-all. Twenty-five seconds later, Darren Belizare scored inside, giving Cambridge-SD a lead it never relinquished the rest of the game. Ennals followed with a layup. Hughes scored inside for a 36-30 Cambridge-SD lead.
Decatur called time and got a layup from Coleman out of the break. But Perkins splashed a 3-pointer and Hughes muscled inside for a score and a 41-32 lead that prompted another Decatur timeout.
"We came in with a great mindset tonight, thinking that we were going to win," Hughes said. "We knew we had to crash (the boards) and get the rebounds tonight because they were taller. We had to box out, play together, play relentless."
Cambridge-SD continued to do all three.
A 7-2 run got Decatur within four at 43-39 with under two minutes to go in the third. But the Vikings answered the last basket of that run, and the Seahawks' other two field goals of the period, to take a 49-43 lead into the fourth.
"Coming into this game everybody said their size was going to be the problem, but in all actuality it wasn't," said Moody, who buried a 3-pointer 1:24 into the final period for a 52-43 Cambridge-SD lead. "We were equally matched up. We boxed out hard. Anthony Hughes got us great rebounds in the stretch. I think that's where we won this game with the rebounds. It didn't come from offense. It came from defense and getting our rebounds.
The Vikings continued to use that combination to their advantage over the final six minutes, forcing turnovers, pounding the glass on both ends, and often limiting the Seahawks to just one shot a possession.
"That's our calling card," Tucker said of his defense. "We just turn people over. Sometimes our offense can get a little stagnant, but we turn people over. That's our offense."
Decatur closed within 55-50 on a Chandler bucket with 3:47 left. Ennals' 3-pointer and a basket by Belizare pushed Cambridge-SD's lead back to 10 at 60-50 with just over three minutes left. Back-to-back baskets by Careen Bolden (10 points) again narrowed the Viking lead to six. But Ennals scored off a Perkins miss and Moody hit two free throws to make it 64-54.
Wise hit a jumper to get the Seahawks within 64-57 with 1:13 left, but the Vikings cemented the win, hitting six of eight free-throw attempts over the final 1:10.
"We've been preaching the last couple of days, and it's been in our scouting report: match their physicality," Tucker said. "And that's what we did tonight. We matched their physicality. Those guys, they're resilient. We had a couple of guys go down that play a lot of minutes, but they still found a way to win this game. I just love those guys' resiliency."

Late surge lifts Wi-Hi past Lions

 SALISBURY — It had been 12 days since its undefeated season was stopped cold via a 40-point shellacking from unbeaten Wicomico.Now, just 11 seconds into the fourth quarter of a seesaw Bayside Conference championship, Queen Anne's County High's girls basketball team was holding a one-point lead over that same Wi-Hi bunch Tuesday night. But the Lions' hopes for a second conference crown in three years virtually evaporated over the next four minutes, as the Indians went on a 13-0 run that proved fuel enough for a 58-52 victory at the Wicomico Youth & Civic Center.
"It was a great game," Queen Anne's head coach Mike Kern said after Wicomico had earned its first conference championship since 1985.
Routed 81-41 by Wi-Hi on Feb. 8, Queen Anne's (19-2) took a quick 5-0 lead Tuesday, prompting Indians head coach Willie Downing to burn a timeout with only 28 seconds elapsed. The Lions never trailed in the first half, and carried a 25-23 lead into halftime.
The game became a back-and-forth contest in the third period, with five lead changes and two ties. A pair of Taylor Jordan free throws pulled Queen Anne's even at 36-36 with 1:08 remaining in the third. But Wicomico sophomore guard Se'Lah Foreman (game-high 26 points) hit a 3-pointer just 12 seconds later for a 39-36 Indians lead.
A transition layup from freshman guard Kariana Hickson (team-high 20 points) with 12 seconds left in the third quarter, and freshman Laila Coles' drive 11 seconds into the fourth nudged Queen Anne's to a 40-39 lead.
But Foreman and Wi-Hi (21-0) took over from there.
In one of the few defensive lapses of the game, Foreman was left alone and canned a 3-pointer with 7:37 left in the game for a 42-40 Wicomico lead. A Lions turnover led to Carlisa Johnson scoring inside. Foreman converted a steal into a layup. Gabrielle Corbin (10 points) then scored on a put-back, giving the Indians a 48-40 lead, drawing a Queen Anne's timeout.
Wi-Hi wasn't quite through.
Another Lions turnover led to an inside bucket from Sariah Sanon. Foreman then got behind the Queen Anne's defense for an easy breakaway layup and a 52-40 lead with a little over four minutes to play.
"What really hurt us is the fourth quarter, leaving Foreman open for that wide-open three, and then she got a couple breakaways," Kern said. "We weren't marked up well and had some mental lapses there, and they got some easy baskets out of it. That turned a one-point (Queen Anne's) lead into a (12)-point (Wi-Hi) lead and it was hard to fight back."
Jordan's basket with 3:44 left ended a four-plus minute Lions' scoring drought, but the Indians answered with baskets from Jecolia Traore (eight points) and Johnson (eight points) for a 56-42 cushion with under three minutes remaining.
"The big thing we talked about at halftime was stop hesitating, because it was like they were overthinking what we were doing," Downing said. "Once they did that part and just started relaxing, the defense picked it up. Once they got active on defense, they didn't have time to think about anything else."
Queen Anne's consistently drove to the basket, but often had shots rejected by Sanon or Corbin, who together accounted for the bulk of Wi-Hi's 15 blocked shots.
"We were hoping to get them in foul trouble and we ended up in foul trouble," said Kern, who watched Coles draw her fourth foul early in the third quarter and RJ Ensor foul out midway through the fourth. "That hurt us a little bit."
The Lions were also hurt at the free-throw line, where they converted 14 of 25 attempts.
"Foul shooting we struggled," Kern said. "If we had shot better it would have been a different score."
Queen Anne's did manage to outscore the Indians, 10-2, over the final 2:48, with freshman Bea Holthaus hitting a free throwing to put the finishing touches on a 15-point, 10-rebound performance.
"I was proud we did fight back," Kern said.

 STEVENSVILLE — There have been seasons when Kent Island High's girls basketball team has beaten opponents from long distance.That hasn't been the Bucs' most common thread to victory this season.
The one-two inside scoring punch of Sydney Riska and Makayla Kropfelder combined for 27 points, and Kent Island went on a 13-0 first-half scoring run Wednesday night to gain separation in an eventual 46-37 victory over North Caroline in a Class 2A East Region II quarterfinal.
The defending region champion, fourth-seeded Kent Island (18-3) advances to Friday's semifinal at top-seeded Wicomico (21-0). Second-seeded Queen Anne's (19-2) hosts No. 3 Parkside (18-3) in Friday's other semifinal.
"We used to be a three-point team and now we're a post team," Bucs head coach David Plumer said. "It's no secret. Everybody who watches film on us will know. But the post-play is getting better. Makayla and Sydney did great tonight. They can complement everybody else. We got the ball inside. We're a little bigger than them and we knew that."
North Caroline (14-7), which came in having won nine of its last 11, took a 6-4 lead a little over 3 minutes into the game, when Chloe Escoe (team-high 14 points) hit the second of her four 3-pointers. But Riska (game-high 17 points) scored on a put-back with 3:09 left in the first quarter to start the Buccaneers on a decisive 13-0 streak.
"We started off moving the ball early," North Caroline head coach A.J. Jackson said. "We had some good offensive possessions, but then we had a drought there where we got sort of undisciplined tonight, and that ended up hurting us later in the game."
The Bulldogs went 9 minutes without a field goal before Ashley Kercheval got behind the defense for a layup with 3:49 left in the first half, cutting Kent Island's lead to 20-8. Riska hit a pair of baskets during the run and Kropfelder (10 points) made a three-point play.
"We knew this was going to be a post-play game," said Riska, who finished with 13 rebounds for her 17th double-double of the season. "So just getting the ball down to me and Makayla, and then just getting the shots up. Obviously we didn't do well from the three-point line, but we did work well in the paint. The outside shots weren't falling for me but I worked inside to get it done."
As did Kropfelder.
"Just trying to make the best plays for my team," the sophomore center said. "If I'm not there, if there's too many defenders, pass it. I missed a couple opportunities but I just need to work on that personally."
Lacy Dauses hit a cutting Riska for a layup and a 23-10 halftime lead. Riska and Kropfelder then teamed to score all the points in a 6-0 burst to open the third quarter, expanding Kent Island's lead to 29-10 less than 3 minutes into the period.
But the Bulldogs outscored the Bucs, 14-4, over the remaining 4:52 of the third quarter to pull within 33-24 entering the fourth quarter.
Kent Island regained its double-digit lead with Lilli Dauses converting a pair of free throws and Kropfelder scoring off a Riska assist for a 37-24 cushion.
"Credit to their bigs," Jackson said. "Second-chance shots, they really battled down there. And the effort on defense, especially when we made a little run there in the fourth quarter. Like hustling, not giving up. That team is well coached. Credit to Plumer."
North Caroline again cut its deficit to under 10 with 5 minutes remaining when Escoe drilled another 3-pointer and Malayah Phillips scored on a layup to make it 37-29. But Kent Island twice worked the ball inside to Riska, who was fouled and hit four consecutive free throws to make it 41-29 midway through the final period.
The Bulldogs wouldn't get any closer than eight the remainder of the game, as their small runs were countered by the Bucs.
"It's always been a little bit of a dogfight," Kent Island guard Caroline Cavanaugh said. "We go in there, we get a lead, they come back. We just need to be a little more consistent with our defense and our offense. They played really well. We just played better this game."

title: ENDING ON A GREAT NOTE
author: Bill Haufe
content:
ENDING ON A GREAT NOTE

 February 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Read News Document

 Gary Gould was admittedly a bit baffled as he kept watch on Beth Tfiloh School's boys basketball team heading toward the postseason."They lost a couple games the last week of the (regular) season," said Saints Peter and Paul High's head coach, whose team had lost three straight to the Warriors. "And then some of the games they won, they only won by like four or five points to teams that we were beating by double-digits. I was confused why other teams could play them so well and we couldn't. And then I thought about it and said, it had to be me. I was doing too much. I was trying to be too good in the x's and o's part, instead of just letting us play."
Gould let his team play Saturday night, made a halftime adjustment, then watched the Sabres pull away in the second half for a 68-58 victory over Beth Tfiloh in the Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference championship game at UMBC's Chesapeake Employers Insurance Arena.
"It feels amazing," said senior forward K'den Spears, named player of the game after Sts. Peter & Paul won its first MIAA C title since 2016. "The only reason why we keep losing games is when we selfishly play. We really played as a group and really helped each other and built each other up."
Though a mid-season injury limited junior star Garett Hemingway's minutes, Sts. Peter & Paul had built a nice hot streak heading into the playoffs, having won nine of its last 10, including its last eight straight.
Beth Tfiloh defeated Sts. Peter & Paul in last year's conference championship, won a two-point nail-biter in Easton on Jan. 11, then rolled to a 72-45 victory at home Jan. 31, dealing the Sabres their most lopsided loss of the season, as well as the only blemish during their hot streak.
But Warriors head coach Ari Braun didn't necessarily put a lot of stock in his team's Jan. 31 romp.
"The first game this year was down to the wire at Saints Peter and Paul. Either team could have won it," Braun said of the Jan. 11 clash in which Hemingway scored 33 points. "The second time, I think that was (Hemingway's) first game back from his ankle and he was not the same player. They weren't all right yet, and we made shots and defended. Obviously we played an awesome game, and it looks worse than maybe it should have."
Then came Saturday night's title bout.
"I think the difference was we were more focused," Gould said. "We realized the game at Beth was something we knew wasn't going to happen again because we didn't shoot the ball well. Plus that second game, I did too much. I was trying to coach too much strategy wise and take away things and add stuff. I think I had my kids playing too slow.
"The kids knew that last year we didn't know what to expect, so we played with a little nerves," Gould said of the Sabres' 65-58 loss in the title game. "But this year we knew going in what to do. So the kids were just focused about getting it done, went out and just played. And we knew it was just our time."
Hemingway (game-high 19 points) canned a pair of 3-pointers early as the Sabres (16-8) carried a 27-24 lead into the locker room after a back-and-forth first half. And while he was guarded against over-coaching again, Gould searched for an edge during the first half.
"I was trying to figure out on the sideline what was happening; what were they doing that was working, and what we could take away to give us the advantage," Gould said.
Gould's key takeaway was switching from the man-to-man and 2-3 zone defenses the Sabres used in the first half to a 1-2-2 zone. The move proved critical, especially when it came to defending Warrior senior guard Michael Cohen, who scored a game-high 35-points in last year's title game.
"Their skip passing wasn't available to them," Gould said. "And then we kept number four, Michael Cohen, in front of us so he wasn't able to penetrate and do all the stuff he did to us last year. He was the guy who hurt us."
Consistently penetrating inside and drawing contact, Cohen went 19 of 28 from the line in last year's final, which included a 12-of-16 effort in the fourth quarter. In Saturday's rematch he finished with 17 points.
"Defense was big for us," Hemingway said. "We came into the game saying, if we can slow them down, hold Cohen. Slow him down, get in front of him, take charges. As long as we get the defense down the offense will just come."
Braun agreed Gould's defensive tweak was big.
"They did an unbelievable job with their defense, Braun said. "They started off in the man, which I didn't think it went great for them, but then they quickly pivoted to the zone. And they were very disciplined in staying back and clogging the paint and not really giving Michael as many opportunities to drive. Last year in the championship game, they were pressing and allowing us to get out in the open court, and that led to a lot of his free throws and baskets. But this year they did a great job of staying at home defensively."
That move produced steals and kick-started the Sabres' transition game. Senior point guard Brayden Smith scored eight of his 13 points in the third quarter, and Robbie Cunningham netted seven of his 11, as Sts. Peter & Paul outscored the Warriors 19-9 for a 46-33 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
Braun, who graduated a number of seniors from last season's title team, acknowledged two other significant factors. Elan Vogelstein, Beth Tfiloh's top rebounder and assist man, suffered a thigh injury in the second Sts. Peter & Paul game, and has been sidelined the remainder of the season.
"I don't know if that changes the outcome of the game, but obviously that would have helped us," Braun said.
And then there was Sts. Peter & Paul's job on the boards, especially the effort delivered by Spears.
"I think what really hurt us even more than the zone was their offensive rebounding," Braun said. "When we can get a stop and end it with a rebound we can then run. That's way different than them getting rebound after rebound and pounding us and then scoring. And then we're just playing against a settled defense. So I thought they just did an awesome job in terms of game plan and execution, just playing with a lot of effort on the court.
"And I think number zero, he was a beast on the glass and our guys really struggled with that," Braun said of Spears.
Spears was a force on the boards in the Sabres' semifinal victory over Cristo Rey. Against the Warriors, he was again tough on the glass, yanking down eight rebounds, and in the score column, finishing with 13 points.
"That's the best I've ever seen K'den play," Hemingway said.
Gould echoed that sentiment.
"He was more consistent and forceful in what he was doing," Gould said of Spears
Spears was also more confident.
"I just felt because this is the second time for us being there, and there was no point in us being nervous because it was the same team we played last year," Spears said.
Beth Tfiloh (25-8) outscored the Sabres, 25-22, in the fourth, but it couldn't rally enough.
"As a team I felt more together," Spears said. "This was our last game and I just wanted to end it off on a really great note."

author: Bill Haufe

Bailey's hot hand fuels Warriors

 EASTON — Wicomico High's defensive plan had held Easton's Marshall Bailey without a field goal for almost three quarters Thursday night.Then in a bid to generate some offense, Indians head coach Butch Waller dropped his triangle-and-two scheme and went man to man. Bailey took advantage of the switch, connecting for 25 of his game-high 30 points over the final 11-plus minutes while leading Easton to a 69-56 victory over Wicomico in a Class 2A East Region II semifinal.
The second-seeded Warriors (15-6) travel to top-seeded Queen Anne's (17-4) on Tuesday for the 2A East Region II championship at 5 p.m. The Lions defeated fourth-seeded Parkside, 62-55, in last night's other semifinal.
"Second half they went man and he was hard to stop," Easton head coach Dionte Hynson said of Bailey. "He was hitting his jump shot, getting to the hole. He put us on his back in the second half."
With the Indians' triangle-and-two limiting Bailey and backcourt mate Ja'Kai Brooks, Easton worked the ball inside to Tymier Thomas (12 points) whose seven first-quarter points helped the Warriors take a 16-10 lead heading into the second quarter.
"They really couldn't get open," Hynson said of Bailey and Brooks in the first half. "Thankfully, Tymier was hitting. He kept us in the game in the first half."
Down 18-12, the Indians rallied to draw even at 18-all on Tyson Hayward's bucket with a little over 5 minutes remaining in the half. Brooks then hit a 3-pointer to break a 22-all tie with 2:06 left before intermission. Kyree Acree (12 points) sandwiched a 3-pointer and a layup around a Zymier Ramirez free throw to push the Warriors lead to 31-25 at halftime.
Waller stayed with his triangle-and-two zone until midway through the third when he opted to go man in hopes of kick-starting his offense.
"We ran a little triangle-and-two and we did an OK job, but we couldn't balance it by scoring," Waller said. "The defense was fine in the first half, even halfway through the third quarter. And then I just said, 'We've got to play them man to man, take our chances, pick the tempo up.' We couldn't do it.
"Same problem we've been plagued with all season long; can't score," Waller continued. "Shooting percentage tonight was 32.1. We've had that same problem, which is understandable with some new players. At this level, or any level really, you've got to be able to put the brown thing in the round thing."
Bailey began doing just that.
After consecutive baskets from Kahlil Batson, and a nice low-post bucket from Acree, Bailey made a three-point play with 3:13 left in the third quarter for a 40-29 Warrior lead. Wi-Hi's Tay'Shawn Swann (16 points) scored on a reverse layup. But Bailey answered with a 3-pointer and another three-point play, extending Easton's lead to 46-32 by the end of the third quarter.
"I just knew we had to lock in defensively because that first half we were only up by six and it was a sloppy game," Bailey said. "So once we locked in defensively — I think we held them to like seven points — everything offensively started clicking for us."
Thomas scored on a drive to maintain the Warriors' 14-point cushion at 48-34 early in the fourth quarter. Bailey then hit back-to-back 3-pointers, drove for a layup and buried a pull-up jumper for a commanding 58-41 lead with 5:13 remaining in the game.
"Excellent shooter," Waller said of Easton's sophomore guard. "One of the better shooters I've seen in years."

 CENTREVILLE — Freshmen Bea Holthaus, Laila Coles and Kariana Hickson have been huge in the Queen Anne's County High girls basketball team's return to the top of the North Bayside this season.Friday night, juniors Lucy Taylor and RJ Ensor showed how big they could be.
Taylor and Ensor combined for nine consecutive points during a 9-2 run to open the second half that staggered third-seeded Parkside while launching the Lions to a 47-31 victory in a Class 2A East Region II semifinal.
Second-seeded Queen Anne's (20-2) travels to Salisbury to face top-seed Wicomico (22-0) on Wednesday at 5 p.m. for the region title. The Indians are the only team to defeat the Lions this season, rolling to an 81-41 victory Feb. 8, and a 58-52 win in the Bayside Conference championship 12 days later.
"I've been trying to find my shot all year it feels like," said Taylor, who led Queen Anne's with 15 points. "But tonight, I don't know. I saw the freshmen, their first year being here (in the playoffs). And being one of the captains I felt like I needed to kind of do something. Kind of step up and keep the encouragement up. It was a really good team win tonight."
Queen Anne's looked like a team that was playing its first game in 10 days, as Jeliah Gardner scored six of her game-high 16 points in the first 4:28 to help the Rams (18-4) to a 10-2 lead.
"Slow start," Lions head coach Mike Kern said. "The first six points were off transition. Then their next couple baskets were backside so we switched to a 2-3."
Coles (11 points) sandwiched a 3-pointer and a layup around two Holthaus free throws to get Queen Anne's within 12-9 by the end of the first period.
Gardner's three-point play extended the Rams' lead to 15-9 with 2 minutes elapsed in the second quarter. But Ensor (eight points, six rebounds, four assists) scored on a drive. Coles snagged a rebound and went coast to coast for a layup before Jordan Taylor scored off an Ensor dish, tying the game at 15-15 with 2:50 remaining in the second quarter.
Gardner scored consecutive baskets to help move Parkside back to a 20-15 lead before Ensor hit a free throw with 5 seconds left to make it a four-point Lions' deficit at the half.
But Taylor and Ensor gave Queen Anne's a quick offensive jolt to start the third quarter. Taylor converted an Ensor pass for an inside bucket. Ensor splashed a 3-pointer. Taylor scored from in close for a 23-20 Lions lead.
Zion Oge scored the Rams' first basket of the second half with 4 minutes left in the third quarter. Taylor answered, taking a Coles feed and scoring inside. TaLayah Clark (nine points) scored, drawing Parkside within 25-24.
But the Rams wouldn't score again until 12 seconds remained in the third quarter, as the Lions dominated the defensive glass, allowing Parkside just one shot time after time.
"Total collapse," Parkside head coach Warren White said after the Rams were held to just six points in the third quarter and five in the fourth. "We've been telling these kids all year, 'You have to play through this mental stuff.
"And free throws killed us," said White, whose team was 3 of 15 from the foul line. "The whole game I don't think we made more than three free throws. That would have kept us in the game."
But Queen Anne's work on the defensive boards helped fuel a 16-6 third quarter and a 15-5 fourth period.
"Defensive rebounding," Kern said. "And that was what our mentality was: one shot and done. So we did better rebounding. We like to press but we kind of just sat back in a 2-3 zone and made it tough. And they shot a lot from the outside. We just got to get the rebound. I don't know how good they were from the three-point line but they weren't very good tonight."
Queen Anne's used a 7-0 run in the closing 2:21 of the third quarter to begin pulling away. Jordan hit a short jumper, Ensor converted a steal into a layup, and Coles sank a pair of free throws before a Taylor free throw capped a 15-4 third-quarter run, giving the Lions a 32-26 lead.
The Lions continued to widen their lead in the fourth, starting with Julia Rendulic, who came off the bench to drain a 3-pointer to start another 9-0 Queen Anne's run.
"Defensively we did well," Kern said. "I think in the second half when RJ hit that three got us going, got us playing with some momentum. Julia comes in and hits a three. Those are the kind of things that are big plays.
"Laila had a couple of good steals, and took it to the basket and got fouled," Kern continued. "And that combination was good. "K-5 (Hickson) was the leading scorer the last two big games we played and she had a little slow night, and so did Bea. But it was good to see Lucy and RJ step up, and Taylor Jordan came off the bench and got a couple big baskets."

Lions survive Easton rally for title

 CENTREVILLE — Jeff Hollis said he wasn't nervous, especially with seniors Vince Gilberto and Collin Woolford in the game."I always feel like with Vince and Collin on the court that somebody's going to make a winning play," said Hollis, Queen Anne's County High's boys head basketball coach.
Hollis was right. Somebody did make a winning play, and that somebody was freshman Jadereon Thompson.
Fouled with 1 second left, Thompson hit the first of two free throws Tuesday night to lift top-seeded Queen Anne's to a 66-65 victory over No. 2 seed Easton in the Class 2A East Region II championship.
The Lions (18-4), who have won six straight since a Jan. 30 loss at Easton, now wait for the Class 2A field to be reseeded, and will likely host a state quarterfinal either Friday or Saturday. Easton finishes the season 15-7.
"Really elated. It's been three years coming to this game and we've lost two of them," said Hollis, whose season was ended by Wicomico the past two years in the region final. "So to finally win one feels really good."
Down 32-31 at halftime, the Lions looked well on their way to victory as they outscored Easton, 22-7, in the third quarter to carry a 53-39 lead into the fourth.
But behind Marshall Bailey, who scored 17 of his game-high 27 points in the fourth quarter, Easton rallied as the sophomore guard scored on a drive with 4 seconds remaining to tie the game at 65-65.
On the ensuing inbounds pass, Gilberto threw a pass three-quarters of the court to Thompson, who drove straight to the basket and was fouled with 1 second left on the clock.
"I was either going to get the layup or get fouled," Thompson said.
During a timeout prior to his free-throw attempts, Thompson said all his teammates came up to him offering him encouragement.
"It felt great," Thompson said. "I had to knock 'em down to win the regional final."
Thompson hit the first, then watched the second attempt bounce and get rebounded by Gilberto to seal the win.
"He's really not a freshman," Hollis said of Thompson. "He's a freshman in age, but he's not a freshman. He's been building to this point. He's just an exceptional kid and an exceptional athlete."
Easton outscored the Lions 26-13 in the fourth quarter.
"I thought we were going to overtime," Warrior head coach Dionte Hynson said. "I'm proud of the kids. Helluva comeback. We had to dig deep. We had to play solid D. I'm not taking anything away from Queen Anne's but our kids played their butts off tonight."
Diontye Copper's 3-pointer with 6:27 left in the third quarter pulled Easton even with the Lions at 35-all. But Queen Anne's outscored the Warriors 18-4 over the final 5:39 of the quarter to build a 53-39 lead, with Woolford (12 points) scoring seven points in the run.
"We just couldn't score any points third quarter," Hynson said.
Bailey, who was 8 of 9 from the foul line, hit a pair of free throws to start Easton's fourth-quarter comeback, drained two 3-pointers and continuously attacked the rim, scoring or drawing contact.
"He's a great player," Hollis said of Bailey. "Hat's off to Easton. I thought their players and their coaching staff did a great job. They weathered the storm when we got up on 'em. They came back.
"But our kids made the final winning play," Hollis added. "We talk about it all the time. Things happen during a game. Who's going to be the man that makes the final winning play. We've had that a couple times this year."
Gilberto had 14 points for Queen Anne's, Nickai Gross and Hollace Branch each had 10, and Thompson finished with nine.
Rayan Haq had 10 for Easton and Kyree Acree eight.

 CENTREVILLE — Friday night's Class 2A boys basketball state quarterfinal playoff between Carver Vo-Tech and host Queen Anne's County High was stopped with 6:57 remaining in the third quarter when an altercation broke out between the two teams that left one Queen Anne's player injured.In a press release late Friday night, the Queen Anne's County Office of the Sheriff said, "it was actively investigating an assault that took place Friday on a Queen Anne's County High School basketball player at the game.
"We have obtained and are currently reviewing video surveillance footage as part of our ongoing efforts," the release stated. "No arrests have been made at this time as we continue to review evidence and fully investigate this incident."
Carver was winning 42-15 at halftime and extended that lead to 47-15, when Dorrian Sands hit a baseline jumper and a 3-pointer in the first minute.
Queen Anne's was approaching mid-court on its ensuing possession when a cross-court pass was intercepted by a Carver player, who drove quickly to the basket and was fouled from behind by Thompson. A Carver player confronted Thompson.
Video footage on Twitter showed players from both teams exchanging words near the Carver basket. Players and coaches from both benches came onto the court. The video then shows the altercation escalating when a Queen Anne's player is punched in the face. It is not clear from the video who struck the Queen Anne's player.
Members of the Queen Anne's County sheriff's department, Queen Anne's school administrators and staff, and both coaching staffs quickly separated players. The game's three officials conferred and decided to officially call the game.
"Our players, teams, community and school staff deserve a safe environment, we have zero tolerance for this type of behavior at our public events, and we can assure our community that this investigation will be thoroughly completed, and appropriate charges will be done at the conclusion," Queen Anne's Sheriff Gary Hofmann said in the press release.
Queen Anne's County athletic director Kwandrey Wilson and head basketball coach Jeff Hollis would not comment on the incident.
Carver advances to the semifinals where it will meet Middletown.
As of Saturday afternoon, it was not known if the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association would take any action on the incident or dole out any punishment.
Queen Anne's (18-4) took a 2-0 lead on a pair of Vince Gilberto free throws 1:23 into the game. The Bears (16-4) rattled off the next nine points before Collin Woolford hit a 3-pointer for the Lions midway through the first quarter.

 SILVER SPRING — Anthony Hughes and Koby Ennals know basketball can be a game of runs.The two juniors were part of the run that mattered most Tuesday night.
A one-time 17-point lead reduced to three, Hughes and Ennals helped fuel a decisive 8-0 fourth-quarter burst that returned momentum back to Cambridge-South Dorchester High's boys basketball team en route to the Vikings earning a 60-53 victory over Fort Hill in a Class 1A state semifinal at Montgomery Blair High School.
Top-seeded Cambridge-SD (24-1) will bid for its first state title since 1996 Friday, when it faces No. 2 seed Edmondson-Westside (22-2) for the Class 1A championship at the University of Maryland's Xfinity Center. Edmondson defeated third-seeded Smithsburg, 79-59, in Tuesday's other 1A semifinal.
"We just got a believe attitude," Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Tucker said. "We told them, 'If we just slow it down we'll be fine. We just got to be patient.'"
The Vikings went on an 11-1 run to open the game, and packaged a 13-2 scoring spree during the second quarter, when they outscored the Sentinels, 23-8, to carry a 37-20 lead into halftime.
"We turned it over way too much in the first half," Fort Hill head coach Thad Burner said. "I thought that their energy was a lot better than ours, particularly in the second quarter when they extended that lead."
Senior point guard LaShaun Moody (team-high 18 points) had a three-point play and a drive that helped Cambridge-SD build its early 11-1 lead. But Fort Hill (19-4) got 3-pointers from DeShaun Brown (team-high 18 points) and Jabril Daniels (10 points) in the final 3:16 of the first quarter to pull within 14-12 heading into the second quarter.
The Vikings led 16-14 when they pieced together a 9-0 run midway through the second quarter. Ennals (13 points), who scored his 1,000th-career point in the first quarter, converted a Moody dish for a bucket off the glass. Semaj Pinder (nine points) hit a turnaround jumper then scored on a drive. Ennals scored on a put-back before Thomas Wilson canned a 3-pointer for a 27-14 Vikings lead.
Brown hit another trey to end a three-plus minute Fort Hill scoring drought. But Moody hit a 3-pointer, Ennals made two free throws, and Darren Belizare scored on a follow before Moody splashed another trey at the buzzer for a 37-20 Vikings lead.
"We preach getting off to a fast start," Tucker said. "We knew Fort Hill was a second-half team and it was going to be a battle. So to get out on a team like that early is huge."
The Sentinels went on an 11-2 run to start the third quarter, getting within 39-31 with 4:36 to go in the period. Hughes stopped that momentum briefly when he converted a steal into a layup, putting the Vikings back up by 10. A pair of Sterling Perkins free throws moved Cambridge-SD to a 44-33 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
Fort Hill came out bombing in the fourth. Landon Sensabaugh hit back-to-back three-balls and Brown turned a steal into a layup, cutting Cambridge-SD's lead to 45-41 with 6:30 left. Tucker called time and watched Hughes score another big bucket inside to make it a six-point lead.
Jabril Daniels answered with another 3, shaving Fort Hill's deficit to three at 47-44 with 5:38 remaining.
But Cambridge-SD showed it too could respond.
"We just had to come back and be ourself," Hughes said. "It's win or go home."
Hughes scored on a put-back. Ennals converted a pair of free throws. Moody scored on a follow before Ennals snatched a rebound and raced coast-to-coast for a bucket that pushed Cambridge-SD's lead to 55-44 with under 4 minutes to play.
"We made some pretty good runs in the third and the fourth, but (number) two (Ennals) and five (Moody), they were pretty good," Burner said.
The Sentinels wouldn't get any closer than nine the rest of the way, as Moody scored on a drive and made three of four free throws in the final 1:24 to cement the victory and Cambridge-SD's first state final appearance since 1996.
"They're a team that's not going to give up," Ennals said of Fort Hill. "But we're a team that's not going to give up either."

title: C-SD locked in for last dance
author: Bill Haufe
content:
C-SD locked in for last dance

 March 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 Read News Document

 When Darnell Dantzler brought his Edmondson-Westside High boys basketball team together for its first practice Nov. 15, he established the same goal he's set the previous 17 seasons as head coach — winning a state title.That same day, Shawn Tucker, starting just his second season as Cambridge-South Dorchester's head coach, provided a string of goals for his team that included winning the North Bayside regular-season title, the Bayside Conference championship, the Class 1A East Region II crown and the state championship.
Tucker and the top-seeded Vikings (24-1) hope to complete that title string Saturday beginning at 1 p.m., when they face the No. 2 seed and defending state-champion Red Storm (22-2) for the Class 1A state championship at the University of Maryland's Xfinity Center.
"You had a lot of good pieces that needed to learn to play basketball together as a team really quickly," Tucker said, recalling his first impression of this season's team. "But there wasn't quite a team."
Tucker has quite a team on his hands now, one that won its first 13 games this season, lost its one and only game to Queen Anne's, then reeled off 11 consecutive wins to earn a shot at the school's first state title in basketball since 1996.
"It's going to be a really, really good challenge," Tucker said of Edmondson. "But I go back to us playing in the Bayside (Conference) championship versus a team like (Stephen) Decatur. It prepared us."
Cambridge-SD fell behind 8-0 to Decatur on Feb. 22, settled itself, then raced to its first outright conference championship since 1996.
The Vikings got off to blazing starts in their state quarterfinal and semifinals wins. The second of those came Tuesday against Fort Hill, when a one-time 17-point lead was whittled to just three with 5:38 remaining. But instead of calling timeout, Tucker let his team continuing playing, and watched as Anthony Hughes came up with two huge steals to spark a decisive 8-0 Vikings run.
"When that kid hit a three, I could have called a timeout," Tucker said of Jabril Daniels' trey that got the Sentinels within 47-44. "And I looked at them and I said, 'Nope.' I'm going to let them play through that because this is the only way they're going to learn this scenario. They know that's me. In that situation, I call a timeout and I don't have any faith in them. So by not calling that timeout, it showed them that I faith in them and they responded."
Now, the Vikings prepare for an Edmondson program that makes its sixth final appearance in Dantzler's 18 seasons at the helm, which include state championships in 2013, '14 and '23.
"First day of practice my goal always is to make it to the state championship, setting goals up as high as you can set 'em," Dantzler said during a phone interview Wednesday. "But sometime being realistic, you might not be as good. But the number one goal is to always win a state championship."
Danztler though wasn't sure the Red Storm would get the chance to defend their title this season.
"I'm really surprised," Dantzler said of reaching the state final. "We had a couple of people that graduated and transferred out. So going into the season I didn't think we were going to make it there. But through playing hard, I'm just happy and fortunate to make it there."
Adding even more meaning to this championship trip for Dantzler is the fact his son, Darnell Jr., is the Red Storm's starting point guard.
"It's been a dream come true," Coach Dantzler said. "Sometimes it's tough trying to draw the line as father and coach, but I wouldn't trade it for the world, just to have the experience of him being a part of my team, and me being part of his success for his high school career."
A 5-foot-9 junior, Dantzler Jr. has averaged 16.5 points and 11 assists a game this season. He is joined in the backcourt by senior Kyrie Sherrod (13.3 points per game). Then there is Edmondson's frontcourt that features 6-8 sophomore forward Chase Foster (19.8 ppg.; 11 rebounds per game) and 6-4 senior forward Josiah Brown (14.5 ppg., 11.5 rpg.).
"They've played hard all season," Coach Dantzler said. "Hopefully we can bring it home when we play."
That is also the hopes of a Cambridge-SD team that has hounded the opposition on defense this season and attacked the boards on both ends of the floor.
Leading the attack has been 5-9 senior point guard LaShaun Moody (25 ppg.) whose quickness has been a problem for opponents on both ends of the court. Moody may run the show, but has plenty of help. Koby Ennals, a 6-5 junior (19 ppg., 10 rpg), can slash to the rim or bury the 3-pointer. And there's the 6-2 Hughes (10 points), who has come up with huge rebounds, steals and buckets throughout the Vikings' run.
Complementing that trio has been a rotation that includes junior Darren Belizare and sophomores Semaj Pinder, Sterling Perkins (12 ppg) and Thomas Wilson, who have more than made their share of big plays throughout this season.
"I hear they're really good," Coach Dantzler said of Cambridge-SD.
Really good, and really locked in, a quality Tucker has praised during this postseason stretch.
"I wish people could be in the locker room for the pre-game speech," Tucker said. "When I say they are zeroed in, they are locked in. And I've never experienced a group of young men that get locked in so fast. Like one minute they can be joking and playing and when we say, 'All right, let's go,' they just locked in immediately. I thought that wasn't something possible, 'cause you know you can get caught turning that switch on and off. When they lock in, they're in. And that's the way we're going to have to be against Edmondson."

title: Vikings' title shot falls shy
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings' title shot falls shy

 March 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports
