 Read News Document

 COLLEGE PARK — Maybe the stage was too big. Or maybe the team from the big city was just too good.Either way, Cambridge-South Dorchester High wasn't going away.
Down 10 in the first quarter, the Vikings rallied to pull even with Edmondson-Westside of Baltimore with under a minute to play in the first half.
Maybe the defending state champions thought an early third-quarter flurry that pushed their lead to 11 was enough to wilt the team from the Eastern Shore. No such luck. Again Cambridge-SD battled back to tie with one quarter remaining.
Certainly the back-to-back 3-pointers that gave the Red Storm a nine-point cushion with less than three minutes left was enough to make their opponent concede. Still no dice, as Cambridge-SD twice cut that deficit to four in the final two minutes.
"They wouldn't quit," Edmondson head coach Darnell Dantzler said of the Vikings.
They wouldn't. But they wouldn't win either.
No. 2 seed Edmondson converted 5 of 6 free throws in the closing 33 seconds Saturday to finally seal a 69-65 victory over top-seeded Cambridge-SD in the Class 1A state boys' basketball championship at the University of Maryland's Xfinity Center.
"Unfortunately, we didn't come out on the right side of the clock and the game," said Cambridge-SD head coach Shawn Parker, whose team finished the season 25-3. "But man, you saw, they fought to the end. And that's what these guys have been doing all year; fighting 'til the end."
Bidding for its first state basketball title since 1996, Cambridge-SD fell behind 14-4 with less than a minute left in the first quarter, when Edmondson's Kyrie Sherrod hit a 3-pointer. Senior guard LaShaun Moody (team-high 17 points, 10 rebounds) scored a layup and a pair of free throws to get the Vikings within six before Xavier Davis (11 points) scored to beat the buzzer and give the Red Storm (26-2) a 17-8 lead after the first quarter.
Down eight, Cambridge-SD pieced together the first of its comebacks. Semaj Pinder (11 points) and Sterling Perkins drained back-to-back 3-pointers before Kobe Ennals (12 points) scored a lay-in to forge a 23-23 tie with 51 seconds left in the first half.
But Chase Foster, Edmondson's talented 6-foot-10 sophomore center who finished with 18 points, 13 rebounds and five blocked shots, hit a pair of free throws before Sherrod drilled a 3-pointer just before the halftime buzzer for a 28-23 Red Storm lead.
Edmondson looked on the verge of taking control in the opening 2:33 of the third quarter, as Ennals picked up his third foul while the Red Storm were in the midst of a 10-4 run that gave them a 38-27 lead with 5:27 to go in the third.
But trailing 39-31, Cambridge-SD again began whittling away its deficit. Moody made a three-point play, then scored on a put-back to make it a three-point game. Darnell Dantzler Jr.'s jumper with 2:07 to go in the third gave the Red Storm a 45-38 lead.
But Darren Belizaire (10 points) hit a trey. Moody made yet another three-point play. Belizaire converted one of two free throws, before Moody zipped one of his five assists to Anthony Hughes for a layup just before the buzzer, tying the game at 47-all entering the fourth.
"Unfortunately, you don't want to get down that big 'cause it takes a lot of energy to come back," Tucker said. "But one word that sticks out to my head is resilient. We're resilient. No matter what, we're going to fight until the end and that's what we did."
Foster's follow nudged the Red Storm back in front at 49-47. Ennals answered with a jumper to create the game's fourth and final tie.
It remained close. But Josiah Brown (13 points) hit two free throws and a 3-pointer before Sherrod nailed a 3 for a 60-51 Edmondson lead with 2:20 remaining.
Pinder's 3-pointer and Hughes' layup off a steal pulled Cambridge-SD within 60-56 with 1:57 left.
"They played hard," Coach Dantzler said. "Even when we went up a couple points they came down and hit a couple big shots."
Dantzler Jr. scored on a drive, extending Edmondson's lead to 62-56. Ennals hit a free throw. Brown scored inside to make it 64-57 Red Storm. But Pinder drilled a 3-pointer with 52 seconds left, getting the Vikings within four again at 64-60.
Brown made one of two free throws with 33.4 seconds left for a five-point edge. Pinder fouled out when he was called for a charge. Ennals tipped the ensuing inbounds pass, but the Vikings could not come up with the ball. A quick foul by Moody sent Foster to the foul line, where he made both free throws for a 67-60 lead with 19.9 left.
Belizaire connected for a 3-pointer with 10.6 seconds left, drawing Cambridge-SD within 67-63. But Dantzler Jr. hit a pair of free throws with 9 seconds to go for a 69-63 advantage.
"It says that we wanted it," Moody said when asked about the Vikings' unwillingness to fold. "We came up a little short but it definitely says that we wanted it."
Tucker agreed.
"When that buzzer went off we just fell a little short," Tucker said. "We competed. We showed everybody in the state of Maryland that we can compete."
It was Edmondson's fourth state championship under Dantzler, and the second time the Red Storm have won consecutive titles, matching the 2013 and '14 teams. But it was the first time Edmondson has won the Baltimore city title and state championship in the same year.
"It just speaks volumes about these kids," said Dantzler, who has coached Edmondson for 18 seasons. "They went undefeated in Baltimore city, they won the city championship, and then to come in and win the state championship. Who could ask for anything more when it comes to these kids? This is the best record I had overall to be 26-2. It's a remarkable season that these guys had."
Dantzler had similar praise for Cambridge-SD.
"I told all of them when we were shaking hands that they played well," Dantzler said. "And I told the coach I know this is only his first year down here, and he's only a second-year coach, but they did a remarkable job."

title: Queen Anne's shuts down Warriors
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's shuts down Warriors

 December 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — While his offense may be the most dynamic he's had in years as Queen Anne's County High's girls head basketball coach, defense has been Mike Kern's greater focus early this season.The Lions gave Easton a heavy dose of both Tuesday night.
Damiya Henry scored 16 points, Karianna Hickson had 14, and Queen Anne's, after yielding 10 first-quarter points, only allowed 10 over the final three quarters on the way to a 52-20 victory over the Warriors.
The Lions improved to 5-0 overall, 3-0 North Bayside, setting up Thursday's early division clash with Cambridge-South Dorchester (4-0, 2-0) in Centreville.
"I'm looking for good defense," said Kern, whose team trailed 10-9 after the first quarter. "We gave up 10 points in the first quarter and then I think we gave up 10 the rest of the game. I think it's one of those things we've got to play good defense. We can't give up easy baskets. We've got to move more, contest every shot."
Ki'Mauri Lewis scored on a drive to give Easton (1-3, 1-1) an early 2-0 lead. Queen Anne's moved to a 5-2 lead, but Serenity Velez buried a 3-pointer and Lewis scored from the baseline for a 7-5 Warriors lead with 3:51 left in the first quarter.
A pair of Hickson free throws and a Laila Coles layup off a backdoor cut nudged the Lions back in front at 9-7 with 2 minutes left in the first. But freshman Maia Bailey connected on a 3 that gave Easton a 10-9 lead heading into the second quarter.
"I thought Easton did a great job driving," Kern said. "We've got to cut the drive off. We've got to slide our feet and get in position.
"They're very athletic," Kern added of Easton. "They pressured us, played us in a man, and it took us a little while to figure it out. And then on the defensive end they were probably a little quicker than we anticipated. We made a couple of adjustments, and I think once we settled down we started playing better."
The Lions did just that while taking control of the game in the second quarter. Hickson scored 12 straight points, which included a pair of 3-pointers, Cheyanne Hollis scored on a putback, and Coles hit a free throw for a 15-0 run that gave Queen Anne's a 24-10 lead.
"Hickson came out big in the first half," Kern said.
Velez hit a basket with 7.3 seconds left in the half for Easton's only points of the quarter.
"Excellent first quarter," Easton head coach Lesley Staehli said of her team. "Then we stopped moving on offense and we got a little lazy on defense. I think that hurt us. We went into halftime with high spirits. Just being within arm's length of them is a positive for us with how good they are. They move the ball well. They cut well."
Queen Anne's maintained its 12-point cushion at 26-14 with 4:24 left in the third quarter.
Then Henry, who played at Easton two years ago and was at Cambridge-SD last season before transferring to Queen Anne's, scored eight consecutive points that extended the Lions lead to 36-14 with 1:10 remaining in the third quarter.
"Henry showed off tonight for sure," Staehli said with a smile of her former player. "Totally miss that kid. Definitely would have done us some good to have her this year. And she went out in two quarters and led the team."
Easton ended a 6-minute scoring drought when Velez canned a 3-pointer with 40 seconds left in the third quarter, making it 36-17 Lions.
Defending North Bayside-champions Queen Anne's then reeled off the first 14 points of the fourth quarter to widen its lead to 50-17 with just under 3 minutes left.
Velez and Bailey each had eight points to lead Easton.
Queen Anne's Bea Holthaus had nine points, 16 rebounds and blocked three shots.

title: Vikings' Hughes adds to big year
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings' Hughes adds to big year

 December 19, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 CAMBRIDGE — It's already been quite a school year for Cambridge-South Dorchester High's Anthony Hughes.As a first-year starting quarterback, Hughes led the Vikings' football team to an undefeated regular season while earning the Bayside Conference Player of the Year.
The senior earned yet another milestone Thursday night, scoring 10 points to reach 1,000 for his career during Cambridge-SD's 73-62 victory over Queen Anne's County.
"It felt great because all my teammates encouraged me to get it," said Hughes, who scored on a tip-in with under 3 minutes remaining for his 1,000th-career point. "They knew I wanted it. I felt like they wanted to get it more than I wanted it myself to get it."
It may have been the toughest 10 points Hughes has scored during his basketball career.
"Kind of felt like I wanted it more than I thought," Hughes admitted. "I was putting too much pressure on myself."
Hughes scored on a 3-pointer with 4 minutes, 38 seconds remaining in the first quarter, but wouldn't score the remainder of the first half. It didn't matter though, as Cambridge-SD (5-0 overall, 3-0 North Bayside) went on a 16-4 tear to close the first half for a 37-24 halftime lead.
Semaj Pinder (17 points) had seven points in the run, starting it with a 3-pointer. Thomas Wilson Jr. (18 points) netted five points, including a 3-pointer during the closing blitz, and Koby Ennals (game-high 20 points) added four points, including a dunk.
"We got back to ourselves," Vikings head coach Shawn Tucker said. "Defense first. That's our motto. And Thomas Wilson Jr. stepped up and hit some big-time shots and that ballooned the lead for us. We were just playing CSD basketball the right way."
A lay-in from Jimmy Holthaus (team-high 19 points) and an Amari Baynard 3-pointer pulled Queen Anne's (4-2, 2-2) within 37-29 in the opening 46 seconds of the second half.
But Wilson buried a trey, scored a layup, hit another 3, and converted a pair of free throws, widening the Vikings' lead to 47-33. Hughes then scored a bucket and made 1 of 2 from the foul line to make it 50-35 with 2:42 left in the third quarter.
The Vikings extended their lead to as much as 60-41 at the end of the third quarter.
But as Cambridge-SD was focusing on trying to get Hughes his milestone on his home floor, its offense began to sputter some, allowing the Lions to slowly close their deficit, as a Chance Hegedus bucket and two Ayden Hicks free throws capped a 14-5 run that drew Queen Anne's within 65-55 with 3:41 left.
But Ennals scored on a drive before Hughes reached his milestone with a tip-in, bumping the Vikings' lead back to 69-55.
"This is a milestone," Tucker said. "We know who we are. We didn't want it (the opportunity for Hughes to score his 1,000th point at home) to slip. We missed some free throws at the end, but those are some things we can correct. The most important thing was for him to have his night, and we were going to do everything in our power for him to get it tonight. And most importantly, we got the W."
But not before Queen Anne's made things a bit more interesting, trimming its deficit to 70-63 on Holthaus' layup with 17.7 seconds left. The Lions would get no closer though, as their three-game win streak was ended.
"I told them, 'We won the second half,'" said Queen Anne's head coach Jeff Hollis, who got 16 points from Baynard and 14 from Hegedus. "We just can't have a second quarter like we did. They outscored 23-8 in the second quarter and that was just too much to come back from."
